newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle active at $65 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle active at $65 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle Wednesday sold at $65.00 per cwt in active trading, up $1.00 from last week's brisk sales, feedlot sources said.

Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma feedlots sold 53,400 head to bring the week-to-date figure to 77,900, including 22,800 formulated and 300 previously contracted cattle to be shipped this week, USDA said.
Kansas feedlots sold 36,000 head, which brought the week to date figure to 40,900, including 3,800 head or about nine percent previously contracted or formulated cattle, USDA said.
Sales in Kansas were lighter because of a strong stance being taken by several feedlots to pass packer bids at $65.00 and price cattle at $66.00, sources said.

Firm beef demand, coupled with current feedlot marketing status, light weights and lower cattle numbers spurred the owner stance for higher money, said Dave Maher, analyst with Securities Corp of Iowa. "It's taking a few more animals to get beef tonnage," Maher said. Average cattle weights for the week ended February 15 were estimated at 1,163 lbs, compared with an estimated 1,164 lbs the previous week and an actual 1,177 a year ago.
